_note: Shot recipes for shots.py (SHOTS.md → Recipes). A shot's "recipe" fills these defaults; anything the shot sets itself wins. Written in our own words from what worked on The Lull, the Cue film and the Higgsfield guides we studied (2026-10-26). camera/realism may use {SNIPPETS} from shots.py's built-ins.

reveal-pullback.note: Opens a film or a scene: start close on one telling detail (a face, an object, the sky), then pull back to show who and where. The reveal is the hook.

lens.focus: deep focus from the subject to the horizon

reveal-pullback.camera: One slow, even dolly-out straight back from the opening detail, on a real track pushed by a grip: level horizon, constant height, the axis on the subject.

chase.note: Speed. The camera flies with the subject. Wide lens = speed: near things streak past while the far background barely moves.

lens.distance: 3 m behind and 2 m above the subject

chase.camera: The camera travels with the subject at its exact speed, close behind and slightly above, banking with it half a beat late, with constant fine turbulence in the frame.

pov-action-cam.note: What the subject sees, from their own eye line. Sells any product that records or sees (a camera, glasses): it shows what the product captures.

lens.look: an ultra-wide action-camera lens, about 150 degrees across, with strong barrel distortion bending the edges

pov-action-cam.camera: A pure first-person view from the subject's eye line, moving with every turn of the head, with constant unstabilised shake.

pan-reveal-smear.note: A gag shot: hold on something far away, pan to bystanders, then the subject tears past in a few frames as a motion-blur smear with one flash of the brand colour, and its wake hits the bystanders.
pan-reveal-smear.camera: A tripod with a fluid head holds on the distant subject, then makes one smooth pan of about forty degrees to the bystanders, eased by a real operator, and holds.

side-track-slowmo.note: Power and grace: a wide side view tracking the subject, centred, in constant slow motion.
side-track-slowmo.camera: The camera tracks alongside at the subject's exact speed, from the side, keeping it in the centre of the frame, steady with a faint live vibration.

telephoto-face-slowmo.note: Effort and emotion in a face, slowed down: a long lens, razor-thin focus, the background melted into colour.

lens.focus: razor-thin focus on the near eye or the product, the background a soft wash

telephoto-face-slowmo.camera: The camera tracks level with the face at the subject's speed, holding one tight side close-up for the whole shot.

aerial-orbit.note: Scale and loneliness: a small figure in a huge place, the world turning behind it.

lens.distance: about 30 m up and 40 m out

aerial-orbit.camera: One slow, stabilised aerial half orbit of 180 degrees around the subject, always aimed at it, at constant speed, the background sliding in deep parallax.

ultrawide-handheld.note: Intimate and immersive: the face huge in the frame while the whole world stays visible around it.

lens.distance: about 50 to 60 cm from the face
lens.focus: deep focus from the face to the horizon

ultrawide-handheld.camera: One long handheld take within arm's length of the subject's face, floating and breathing with a real body, drifting between profile and three-quarter, never cutting away.

top-shot.note: Calm and clear: hands at work on a surface (a map, a desk), seen from straight above.

lens.focus: deep focus across the whole surface

top-shot.camera: Perfectly overhead, looking straight down at 90 degrees, the surface square to the frame, locked off and completely still like a photograph.

natural-packshot.note: The product shot inside a real moment, never posed: someone takes it off, folds it, picks it up mid-conversation, without looking at it.

lens.focus: a macro look, very shallow depth of field, the product razor-sharp and the background soft bokeh

natural-packshot.camera: A slightly shaky handheld extreme close-up at about 45 degrees to the product, travelling with it through the gesture and keeping it large and sharp the whole time.
locks: The product's reflections show the surroundings, never a person.

telephoto-shore.note: A long lens from far away compresses the background into a towering wall behind the subject (a wave, a cliff, a crowd).
telephoto-shore.camera: A long-lens pan from a fixed position, following the subject across the frame and keeping it centred, with only a faint long-lens vibration.

product-answers.note: A feature shown by talking, not graphics: the subject asks the product out loud and a calm voice answers from it. Lip-sync needs Seedance; on H3 the line becomes a subtitle or a voiceover.
audio: a calm, friendly voice answering from the product, close, like a small speaker near the ear

fpv-hatch.note: Ours, from The Lull (S01): a free-flying camera creeps toward an opening, then bursts through it into the open.

kitchen-pushin.note: Ours, from the Cue film (plate 1): a lived-in interior, a documentary operator pushing in toward the hands at work.
kitchen-pushin.camera: Handheld camera, slightly unsteady and organic, like a documentary operator.

selfie-card.note: Ours, from the Cue film (the carousel cards): a phone held at arm's length, talking to camera.

lens.look: a phone front camera at arm's length, slight wide-angle distortion
